newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria MP slams Zagreb for move against radio.
newsitem.headline: Austria MP slams Zagreb for move against radio.

text.p: A senior Austrian parliamentarian on Thursday criticised the Croatian government for its plan to close down an independent radio station, warning Zagreb it was treading a dangerous path away from a democratic Europe.

Greens deputy Terezija Stoisits said the closure of Radio 101, a mouthpiece for free speech when Croatia was part of former communist Yugoslavia, was an offence against freedom of opinion and the freedom of the press.

"Democracy without free media is today no longer possible," Stoisits said in a statement. The Croatian government is "treading a dangerous path which will distance the country even further from a democratic Europe".
Thousands of people demonstrated in Zagreb on Wednesday to protest against the government's plan to award the radio's frequency to a rival station which does not yet exist.
Stoisits said the Croatian government was attempting to eliminate one of the last critical press outlets in the country.
"Not even the Yugoslav communist authorities went that far," she said.
